findings.finding: The Q4 guide assumed ~$3.00/gal all-in and MXN 17.6. Delta now guides Q4 at ~$4.25/gal, and USD/MXN is ~18.3-18.4 in mid-October. On ~120M Q4 gallons the fuel gap alone is ~$120-150M, about 7-9 points of the 15.5-18.5% Q4 operating-margin guide before recapture, or roughly 2-3 points net at a 75% recapture. A reset of the Q4 and FY (11-13% op margin) outlook, or a withdrawal, is very likely on the 10-20 call. Delta cut FY EPS from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60 on the same cause.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In April Aeromexico guided Q2 down on fuel (Q1 print, 2026-04-21 amc). The next-session move is not sourced; the baseline's 04-23 row is -4.92% but may be a traffic day. Delta's 2026-10-09 FY cut on fuel traded about -3%. findings.finding: Demand and capacity sit inside or above the Q3 guide. Q3 ASMs by month were July -1.5%, August +2.3% and September +3.4%, about +1.3% for the quarter against the +0.5-1.5% guide. RPMs were -1.9%, +2.9% and +3.6%. Load factor was 88.0%, 89.7% (+0.6pp) and 87.1% (+0.1pp). September international RPMs grew +6.6% on +6.3% capacity, and management called forward bookings 'healthy'. Together with US airfares up 23% y/y and Delta's +14% yield, this supports revenue at or above the $1.62bn top end through fuel recapture.

findings.finding: Q3 mortgage volume ran below the July guide's assumption. The guide assumed 'current mortgage rates', with the 30-year at about 6.6%. Freddie Mac's 30-year then rose to 6.76% (Sep 10) and 7.03% (week of Sep 24). In August, Optimal Blue rate-and-term refi locks fell 47% YoY and total locks 3% YoY; MBA refi applications were 25% below a year earlier in early September. PennyMac funded $16.6B in Jul-Aug against $34.9B in Q2 (about 28% below Q2's monthly pace). The comparison is tough: Sept 2025 had a refi wave and Q2 2026 hard mortgage inquiries were only +1%. Q3 US mortgage revenue (guided +20%, mostly FICO price pass-through) and EPS therefore likely land at or below the low end of $2.15-2.25. Purchase locks held up (+6% YoY in August), which cushions the shortfall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): adj EPS $2.25 beat $2.20 on +40% USIS mortgage revenue and the stock still fell 3.93% close-to-close on the guide. findings.finding: The Q4/FY26 guide is likely trimmed. The 30-year was 7.28% on Oct 1 and 7.40% on Oct 8 and Oct 15, against about 6.6% when the July guide (FY adj EPS $8.39-8.69, built on 'current rates') was set. The 10-year has been above 5%, and the MBA's September forecast assumes two more Fed hikes. Unless the AI cost savings ($150M run-rate, 2026 portion already in the guide) and EWS diversified growth fill the gap, the FY midpoint ($8.54, against about $8.55 consensus) moves toward or below the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line EFX trades on. July 2026: Q3 guide below consensus, -6.9% to -8.5% premarket and -3.93% at the close. April 2025: a firmer guide in a tariff scare, +13.84%. Feb 2025: a weak FY guide, -8.42%.

findings.finding: The FHFA bi-merge decision is still pending going into the call. Director Pulte, expected to announce it at MBA Annual on Oct 12, withdrew from the conference, and no directive has been found since. Management will have to frame bi-merge and VantageScore exposure for 2027 on the call; on Sept 14 it was defending tri-merge.

If it was not accrued earlier, it is a Q3 GAAP charge that is excluded from adjusted EPS, so it makes a GAAP headline miss possible with no path to the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line. The stock rose 6.17% on 2026-08-19, the day the settlement was reported (also dividend day).

findings.finding: Offsets outside mortgage that the call can lean on. On Sept 14 management cited $100M of new government ACV plus $200M of renewals and a government pipeline double last year's.
